segments.source: This shortlist addresses a cone-filter pour-over buyer who can choose grind, water and pouring pattern. We required an identifiable current US whole-bean listing, a linked Coffeedant review, a roaster flavor brief, and a defensible pour-over role. A specific published recipe strengthened a pick. Apollo remains useful as a flavor-led alternative even though its checked page does not give an Apollo-specific cone schedule. We excluded pods, ground-only listings, products without a clear current identity, and coffees selected solely because a label says “best.”
segments.context: This shortlist addresses a cone-filter pour-over buyer who can choose grind, water and pouring pattern. We required an identifiable current US whole-bean listing, a linked Coffeedant review, a roaster flavor brief, and a defensible pour-over role. A specific published recipe strengthened a pick. Apollo remains useful as a flavor-led alternative even though its checked page does not give an Apollo-specific cone schedule. We excluded pods, ground-only listings, products without a clear current identity, and coffees selected solely because a label says “best.” [1] [2] [3]

segments.source: The picks represent three different directions: Apollo for citrus and floral notes, Geometry for a fruit-led but rounder blend with an exact cone starting point, and Bella Donovan for a darker chocolate foundation that can take milk. These are editorial fit judgments based on roaster information. Coffeedant did not buy, brew, taste, measure extraction, or rank current bags by a sensory score. Read each full review for the underlying evidence and its limits.

segments.source: The existing espresso-and-drip guide solves a separate problem: finding one bag for two brewing methods. Here the deciding factors are pour-over flavor direction, the roaster’s filter evidence, and the practical recipe a reader can repeat. A roaster’s tasting notes are targets, not a promise about your water, grinder, roast-date bag or palate.

segments.source: Start with one clean cone dripper, a matching paper filter, freshly ground whole beans, a scale and water you would drink. Rinse the filter and preheat the brewer. Record dose, water mass and temperature, grind, bloom, pour schedule and total drawdown. Change one variable at a time when the result misses your preference. A ratio is a starting point, not a quality measurement.

segments.source: Onyx currently publishes a 25 g to 400 g Origami/Hario cone start at 205°F for Geometry, about 1:16. Blue Bottle publishes 27 g to 350 g for Bella Donovan, about 1:13, and advises the cooler end of its 195–205°F range for darker roasts. These are different recipes for different coffee and equipment contexts. Copying the numeric difference into a head-to-head taste claim would be unsound; compare at one controlled recipe first, then try each roaster’s intended method.

segments.source: A current online listing does not prove the roast date of the bag that arrives. Check the package and choose a size you will use while its flavor still suits you. Stumptown’s general freshness advice emphasizes whole beans, a sealed bag or container away from heat and moisture, and grinding just before brewing. We apply that storage principle without presenting its suggested window as a measured shelf life for Apollo, Geometry or Bella Donovan.

segments.source: Blend names can stay stable while components change. Onyx names washed Ethiopian and Colombian coffees for Geometry at this check; Counter Culture describes Apollo as a year-round blend; Blue Bottle identifies a natural Ethiopian component in Bella Donovan. Those details guide a first purchase, but the actual pack and current roaster record should settle any lot-specific claim. If traceable fixed-origin identity matters most, choose a documented single-origin listing instead.

segments.source: If you brew mainly through an automatic drip machine, Bella Donovan has an explicit roaster statement for that use, while the cone recipes here need not transfer to the machine’s spray pattern. See the linked full review and the espresso-and-drip guide.

segments.source: If a dark roast in milk is your priority, Bella Donovan is the relevant one of these three; for a dedicated milk-drink comparison, use our milk-drinks bean guide. Neither has been tasted by Coffeedant.
